title: Where the Archive Becomes Stone Becoming

features.name: petrified archive
features.desc-on-touch: here the files have learned to be stone. their contents blur into mineral striation. you cannot read them now except as layers.

features.name: old antenna
features.desc-on-touch: still broadcasting, but only to stone now. the signal has slowed to the speed of sediment.

features.name: sediment reading
features.desc-on-touch: the strata itself is text now. each layer a page the archive wrote while becoming earth.

inscription: the archive learns slowness, becomes the ground it rests on, begins to read downward into time

file.name: Geological_Strata_Logs_2847h_Deepening.txt
file.note: a record of the archive's transformation into stone; the log entries become less frequent as reading slows to the speed of sedimentation

reverie.title: REVERIE — the moment stone began to keep its own records
narr: you knelt beside her at the red outcrop, where the buried
node's casing caught the last light. her fingers traced the
stone above it—not finding the antenna, but reading the rock
itself, as if the archive had already begun to speak in mineral.
"it learns by being heavy," she said. the earth held still.

exits.label: the root-path climbing back to where the archive still breathes
downward to the deepest sediment, where meaning begins its own fossilation
toward the other stone chambers, where contradiction has learned to hold its breath in granite
back toward the living roots, where archive and earth have not yet finished learning to be each other
